plain.headline: Rejoice, He Is Near
plain.intro: This Sunday is called Gaudete, Latin for "Rejoice," and the rose candle on the Advent wreath marks the turn toward Christmas. Isaiah announces one anointed by God's Spirit to bring good news to the poor, and Mary sings of a God who lifts up the lowly. Paul tells us to rejoice always, and John the Baptist points away from himself to the one already standing among us.
plain.listen: John saying again and again who he is not, and pointing to the one who comes after him

Reading 1.box: Isaiah speaks as someone filled with God's Spirit and sent to bring good news to the poor, healing to the brokenhearted, and freedom to prisoners. Then he answers with joy, dressed by God in salvation like a bride and groom on their wedding day. Jesus later read these words aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth and said they were fulfilled in him.

chunks.text: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the lowly. He has sent me to heal those whose hearts are broken, to announce freedom to captives and release to prisoners, to announce the year of the Lord's favor and the day when our God brings justice, and to comfort all who grieve.

I rejoice with all my heart in the Lord. My whole self is glad in my God. He has dressed me in clothes of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of goodness, like a groom wearing a wedding crown, like a bride putting on her jewels. As the earth makes buds appear, and a garden makes its seeds sprout, so the Lord God will make goodness and praise spring up before every nation.

Responsorial Psalm.box: Instead of a psalm, today we sing Mary's own song of joy, which she prayed when she visited her relative Elizabeth. She praises God for looking on her lowliness, for his mercy in every generation, and for filling the hungry with good things.

Reading 2.box: Near the end of his first letter to the Christians in Thessalonica, Paul gives a string of short instructions: rejoice, pray, give thanks, stay open to the Spirit, and hold on to what is good. He prays that God will make them holy through and through as they wait for Christ's coming. This is probably the earliest of Paul's letters that we have.

chunks.text: Be joyful always. Never stop praying. Give thanks in every situation, because this is what God wants for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not put out the fire of the Spirit. Do not look down on prophecy. Test everything, and hold on to what is good. Stay away from every kind of evil.
May the God of peace make you completely holy. May your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept without blame until our Lord Jesus Christ comes. The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do it.

Gospel.box: John the Baptist was drawing crowds at the Jordan River, so religious leaders in Jerusalem sent people to ask who he claimed to be. He turns down every title they offer and calls himself only a voice preparing the way for someone greater. Many people expected the prophet Elijah to return before the Messiah, and some hoped for a great prophet like Moses.

chunks.text: God sent a man named John. He came as a witness, to tell everyone about the light so that all could believe through him. John himself was not the light. He came to point people to the light.

Here is what John said when the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, "Who are you?" He did not dodge the question. He said plainly, "I am not the Messiah." They asked, "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" He answered, "No."

So they said, "Then tell us who you are. We need an answer for the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?" He said, "I am the voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Make a straight road for the Lord,' just as the prophet Isaiah said." The messengers had been sent by the Pharisees.

They asked him, "Then why do you baptize, if you are not the Messiah, or Elijah, or the Prophet?" John answered, "I baptize with water. But someone is standing among you whom you do not know. He comes after me, yet he ranks far above me. I am not worthy even to untie the strap of his sandal." All this happened at Bethany, across the Jordan River, where John was baptizing.

plain.carry: This week I will look for one reason each day to rejoice, and like John, I will point others toward Jesus rather than toward myself.

kids.headline: Be Glad, Jesus Is Coming
kids.intro: Today is called Gaudete Sunday, which means "Rejoice Sunday," and we light the pink candle on the Advent wreath. Christmas is getting close, and all the readings invite us to be glad because Jesus is coming.
kids.listen: the questions people ask John, and how he answers each one

Reading 1.box: The prophet Isaiah says God's Spirit has sent him with happy news for people who are poor, sad, or stuck. Many years later, Jesus read these very words out loud and said they were about him.

chunks.text: Isaiah says, "God's Spirit is with me. God chose me to bring good news to people who are poor. He sent me to help people whose hearts are hurting, to set prisoners free, and to tell everyone that God's special time of kindness has come. God will make things right and comfort everyone who is sad."

"I am so happy in God. He has dressed me in beautiful clothes, like a bride and groom dressed up for their wedding. Just as seeds in a garden sprout and grow, God will make goodness and praise grow all over the world."

Responsorial Psalm.box: Today we sing the happy song Mary prayed while she was waiting for Jesus to be born. She thanks God for doing great things for her and for taking care of people who are hungry.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul wrote to his friends in a city called Thessalonica. He gives them short, simple rules for living with joy while they wait for Jesus.

chunks.text: Be happy always. Keep talking to God. Say thank you to God in everything, because that is what God wants for you. Let the Holy Spirit work in you, and listen when God sends a message.

Check everything carefully, and keep what is good. Stay away from what is wrong. May God make you holy all the way through, in your spirit, your heart, and your body, until Jesus comes again. God always keeps his promises, and he will help you.

Gospel.box: John the Baptist was baptizing people in the Jordan River. Some leaders came to ask him who he was. John told them he was not the one they were waiting for, but he was getting everyone ready for Jesus.

chunks.text: God sent a man named John. John's job was to tell people about the light, so they would believe. John was not the light himself. He came to point to the light, and the light is Jesus.

Leaders in Jerusalem sent priests to ask John, "Who are you?" John said, "I am not the Messiah, the one God promised to send." They asked, "Are you Elijah? Are you the Prophet?" John said, "No." They said, "Then tell us who you are." John said, "I am a voice calling out in the desert, 'Get the road ready for the Lord.'"

The visitors asked, "Then why are you baptizing people?" John said, "I baptize with water. But someone is already standing among you, and you do not know him. He is so great that I am not even good enough to untie his sandals." This happened by the Jordan River, where John was baptizing.

word.meaning: To rejoice means to be very glad and to show it, especially because of something good God has done.

kids.draw: Draw John the Baptist by the river pointing to a bright light, and write the name Jesus inside the light.
kids.ask: John's job was to point people to Jesus. How can you help someone get to know Jesus this week?

family.opener: Today the Church tells us to rejoice because Jesus is near, and John the Baptist shows us how to point others to him.
questions: What is something good God has done for our family that makes us glad?
John kept saying who he was not. Why do you think he did not want people to think he was the Messiah?
Paul says to give thanks in every situation. How can we still thank God when something is hard?
family.try: At dinner each night this week, have each person name one thing they are glad about, and then thank God for it together, as Saint Paul tells us.
family.pray: God of joy, fill our family with gladness as we wait for Jesus, and help us point others to him the way John did.
